title: Spending policies: who and what can consume Copilot Credits, and up to how much
summary: The spending-policy controls, billing rules and documented limitations are supported by Microsoft documentation. The page correctly qualifies the beta API and reports Microsoft's inconsistent License Administrator guidance rather than resolving it by assumption.

claims.claim: Default spending-policy activation starts in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Cost Management > Get Started.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot and then the Cost Management node. ... To unlock AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing, select Get Started.

claims.claim: No documented automation call is identified as equivalent to activating the default policy in this setup experience.
claims.quote: Searched: "activate" "default spending policy" "API"; read setup, Graph overview/create and Partner Center usage-based billing. Graph creates disabled policies; Partner Center says API syntax for getting and creating a spending policy isn't available yet.

claims.claim: Identity policy creation uses Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy. ... Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates an identity-based spending policy.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies

claims.claim: An identity policy's scope, services, billing method, spending limits and alerts can be edited through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Save changes.
claims.quote: Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... Scope ... Agents and services ... Billing method ... Spending limits ... Alerts, and Email alert settings ... select Save changes

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates the policy properties specified in the note, not scope, services or alerts.
claims.quote: PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} ... The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: Policy alerts are reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Alerts, and Email alert settings.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... Alerts, and Email alert settings

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings configures policy alert thresholds.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings ... Create or update the alert configuration.

claims.claim: Resource policy creation starts in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy. ... Enter a name for the policy, then select Resources as its scope.

claims.claim: No Graph call for resource-based Copilot Studio spending policies is documented in the material searched.
claims.quote: Searched: "resource-based" "spending" "Graph"; Copilot spending policy activate default policy API PowerShell resource-based environments Graph. Read Studio costs, Graph overview and create: only allUsersSpendingPolicy and selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy are documented.

claims.claim: A policy is deleted in Microsoft 365 admin center through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > More actions beside the policy > Delete.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab. ... From the list of spending policies, locate the spending policy that you want to delete. ... Select the More actions menu (⋮) next to the spending policy. ... Select Delete.

claims.claim: DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} removes a spending policy.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... Delete spendingPolicy ... DELETE /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} ... Delete a spending policy.

claims.claim: The default activation procedure requires signing in as Global administrator or Billing administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center with one of the following administrator roles: ... Global administrator ... Billing administrator

claims.where: controls[].note; Risks and limits: The API is beta
claims.claim: The documented Cost Management APIs are beta, subject to change and unsupported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy through Graph supports delegated work or school permissions, not application permissions.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All ... Application | Not supported.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The API is beta
claims.claim: Updating a spending policy through Graph supports delegated work or school permissions, not application permissions.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All ... Application | Not supported.

claims.claim: A policy created by the Graph create operation starts disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created disabled.

claims.claim: The Graph create call requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator at runtime.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: The create request supplies a concrete @odata.type.
claims.quote: the request body must set a concrete @odata.type, either #microsoft.graph.allUsersSpendingPolicy or #microsoft.graph.selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy

claims.claim: The create request sets displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.

claims.claim: The create request can select funding through billingMethods.
claims.quote: You can optionally supply billingMethods and billingInstrument. ... "billingMethods": "prepaidCredits"

claims.claim: The update operation changes displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and billingMethods.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: The update request requires the policy ETag in If-Match.
claims.quote: If-Match | The ETag of the spending policy. Required.

claims.claim: Changing non-pay-as-you-go funding to include payAsYouGo requires billingInstrument.
claims.quote: When billingMethods changes stored funding from non-pay-as-you-go to a value that includes payAsYouGo, including prepaidCredits,payAsYouGo, also supply a billingInstrument

claims.claim: That billingInstrument must contain billingSubscriptionId, billingResourceGroup and billingRegion.
claims.quote: with all three writable coordinates: billingSubscriptionId, billingResourceGroup, and billingRegion.

claims.claim: The Graph alert request sets isEnabled and thresholds.
claims.quote: "isEnabled": true, "thresholds": [ { "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.percentageCostManagementAlertThreshold", "value": 80 } ]

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Spending policies are administrator-defined rules controlling access to credit-billed AI experiences.
claims.quote: Use spending policies in the Cost Management dashboard to control access and Copilot Credit spending for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing.

claims.where: summary; What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Each policy selects the agents and services permitted to consume credits under it.
claims.quote: Select the agents and services that users and groups in this policy can access. ... Use the check box to select the agents and services that can consume credits against the billing method tied to this policy.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: A policy can impose a monthly Copilot Credit spending limit.
claims.quote: Limited monthly budget: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot Credits are billed to the subscription selected in the policy billing method.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are billed to the subscription that you select in the billing method.

claims.where: What it is; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Spending policies limit consumption rather than purchasing, reserving or allocating credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies only define access and spending limits, not credit allocation. ... Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity-based policy usage follows the person using selected services.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity policies can cover all users or specific groups.
claims.quote: By default, All users is selected. To target this rule to a subset of users, switch to Specific groups and select the directory group. You can also select multiple groups.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity policies support a per-user monthly limit.
claims.quote: Specify the maximum credit limit users can spend per month.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Resource-based policies manage Copilot Studio usage by agent or environment rather than the user's identity.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want usage to follow an agent or environment rather than the identity of the person using it.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy; controls[4]
claims.claim: Resource policies can cover specific agents, specific environments or all environments.
claims.quote: Specific resources ... Select the agents you want to manage ... Specific environments ... Select one or more environments ... All environments: All existing environments and automatically includes new environments.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy; controls[4]
claims.claim: Resource policies support per-agent limits.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: A group using Cowork is a documented identity-policy scenario.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services. For example, a group using Cowork.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: An existing identity-based policy cannot be converted into a resource-based policy.
claims.quote: You can't convert an existing identity-based policy into a resource-based policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The default setup targets the entire organisation and all users.
claims.quote: The default setup targets your entire organization and all users.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Activating usage-based billing unlocks experiences gated by it.
claims.quote: This process activates AI experiences, like Cowork, that are gated by usage-based billing.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Additional policies have independent limits and do not inherit the tenant-level limit.
claims.quote: Each additional spending policy that you create has its own independent limit and doesn't inherit the tenant-level limit.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The per-user limit is optional in the admin setup.
claims.quote: Select monthly budget limits for users (optional).

claims.where: What it is: How it works; What to check
claims.claim: Policies support alert thresholds and designated email recipients.
claims.quote: Specify the usage threshold for the policy. ... Select the administrators or stakeholders who must receive email notifications when policy usage reaches the threshold.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is on by default for spending policies.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Auto-apply automatically adds future supported services and agents to the policy.
claims.quote: When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Auto-apply; What to check
claims.claim: Turning off Auto-apply requires administrators to review and add new services manually.
claims.quote: When the setting is off, future services and agents aren't automatically included. Administrators must review and add the new services and agents to the policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: For a user in multiple policies for the same service, the highest per-user limit wins first.
claims.quote: If a user is in more than one policy for the same service, the system assigns the user a policy based on the following order: 1. Highest per-user limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A tie in per-user limits is resolved by the largest overall policy limit.
claims.quote: If tied, the largest overall policy limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A remaining tie is resolved by the most recently created policy.
claims.quote: If still tied, the most recently created policy

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: When a policy has no per-user limit, its overall limit is the per-user value used in this comparison.
claims.quote: If a policy doesn't have a per-user limit set, the system uses its overall policy limit as the per-user value for this comparison.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits: Overlapping policies
claims.claim: The selected policy applies in full rather than combining settings or limits from overlapping policies.
claims.quote: The chosen policy applies in full and settings from other policies aren't combined.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: For covered Copilot Studio usage, Microsoft 365 admin center policies take precedence over Power Platform admin center controls.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Within Microsoft 365 admin center, a Copilot Studio resource policy takes precedence over an identity policy.
claims.quote: Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, a policy for the agent or its environment takes precedence over a policy for the person using the agent.

claims.claim: The documented initial usage-based billing setup includes activating the default policy before adding further policies.
claims.quote: Before you create additional spending policies, complete the initial usage-based billing setup and activate the default spending policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends setting a per-user limit to prevent runaway consumption by one user.
claims.quote: Although this selection is optional, review and set this option for your organization to prevent runaway spending of Copilot Credits by one individual user.

claims.claim: Don't limit monthly spending allows the policy to use credits against its billing method without a policy-level ceiling.
claims.quote: Don't limit monthly spending - Allows the policy to use credits against the organization's billing method without restrictions.

claims.claim: Moving Copilot Studio cost management into Microsoft 365 admin center is opt-in through a resource policy.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy.

claims.claim: Existing Power Platform configuration remains in effect until a resource policy covers the environment.
claims.quote: Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits; controls[4].note
claims.claim: For covered resources, Microsoft 365 credit management replaces Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.claim: Usage-based billing charges actual consumption measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: When credits for the selected subscription run out, usage continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.
claims.quote: When credits run out for that subscription, usage automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: When capacity packs and a subscription with Copilot Credit P3 are both selected, billing order is capacity packs, P3, then pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: If you select both Prepaid Capacity packs and an Azure subscription with Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3), billing is applied in the following order ... Prepaid Capacity packs ... Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3) ... Pay-as-you-go billing

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Global and Billing administrators can choose different billing methods per policy for departmental billing.
claims.quote: If you're a Global administrator or a Billing administrator, you can override this selection and select how this policy should be billed. This feature enables you to do departmental billing and vary billing methods for each group, department, or set of users.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists Cowork as requiring a Copilot licence, so policy coverage does not itself settle service licensing.
claims.quote: Cowork (Copilot license required)

claims.claim: The spending-policy documentation read does not state per-service credit rates.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot spending policies credit rates identity based limit change take effect timing. Read setup, managing credits, Studio costs and usage-based billing overview; they describe limits and billing methods, referring licensing details to the Copilot Credits Guide, without per-service rates.

claims.claim: Consumption's cost is an estimate that may not match the bill.
claims.quote: Cost: The estimated cost of your AI usage in local currency, including negotiated rates. It includes usage paid for with prepaid credits and with pay-as-you-go, so it might not match your bill.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit; Governance controls: Interaction
claims.claim: Users hitting the spending limit lose access to agents and services for the remainder of the month.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: Credits reset on the first of the month.
claims.quote: until credits reset on the first of the month

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit; Governance controls: Watching
claims.claim: Users reaching a limit can request more credits.
claims.quote: When users reach their limit within a policy, they can request more credits

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: Reaching a limit does not cause the user to fall back to another policy.
claims.quote: they don't default to other policies. The system keeps the user on the assigned policy and doesn't reevaluate the user against other policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: A running task exceeding the per-user limit can finish without interruption.
claims.quote: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: That excess usage does not count toward the policy limit.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft describes that excess as not billed at Microsoft's sole discretion.
claims.quote: isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion)

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: That excess usage does not appear as consumed credits in Cost Management dashboards.
claims.quote: doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards (Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management)

claims.where: Risks and limits: All environments; What to check
claims.claim: Choosing All environments applies resource-policy management to every environment in the tenant.
claims.quote: Selecting All environments makes this change for every environment in the tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: All environments; Open questions
claims.claim: A newly linked environment can take up to 12 minutes to receive the resource policy.
claims.quote: After you link an environment to a Microsoft 365 spending policy, allow up to 12 minutes for the new policy to apply.

claims.claim: Removing the environment or deleting its resource policy automatically restores the applicable Power Platform policy.
claims.quote: If you remove an environment from a spending policy or delete the resource-based spending policy, the applicable Power Platform admin center policy resumes for that environment automatically.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 resource policies do not cover AI Builder features or their credits.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises against moving resources using AI Builder into these policies.
claims.quote: Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.claim: Moving groups does not reset a user's consumption; prior usage counts against the new policy limit.
claims.quote: Credits consumed under the previous spending policy remain part of the user's consumption history and are accounted for when enforcing the spending limit under the new policy.

claims.claim: After a group move, Consumption's user-level view displays only current usage against the current policy.
claims.quote: Only the current usage against the current spending policy is displayed at a user level in the Consumption tab view.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Coverage is by service list
claims.claim: Microsoft maintains a list of services managed by usage-based billing and says it will extend that list.
claims.quote: Microsoft will add more agents and services over time and provide notifications and updated content as they become available. ... Services managed by usage-based billing in the Microsoft admin center now include:

claims.where: Risks and limits: Coverage is by service list
claims.claim: Microsoft points to separate pay-as-you-go documentation for Copilot Chat, SharePoint agents and the Retrieval API.
claims.quote: For Copilot Chat, SharePoint Agents, or Microsoft Copilot Retrieval API (Preview), see Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go service overview.

claims.claim: Global administrators and Billing administrators can create spending policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center with one of the following administrator roles: ... Global administrator ... Billing administrator ... You can now add more spending policies

claims.claim: AI administrators can edit policies, limits, alerts and billing methods but cannot create policies.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: The setup page grants License administrators policy, limit, alert and billing-method editing but not policy creation, subject to the inconsistency disclosed immediately afterward.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: Supported reader roles including AI Reader and Global Reader have read-only consumption access rather than configuration permissions.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports. These roles provide read-only access to consumption information

claims.claim: The same setup page inconsistently includes License Administrator among read-only roles that cannot edit policies.
claims.quote: License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles ... don't allow administrators to create or change spending policies, limits, alerts, request policies, or billing methods.

claims.claim: An existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role.
claims.quote: an existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role

claims.claim: Alerts notify rather than enforce spending limits.
claims.quote: Configure notify-only threshold alerts and manage their recipients.

claims.claim: Alert emails start when usage reaches the threshold and repeat daily until the monthly period resets or the policy is adjusted.
claims.quote: Alert emails begin when usage reaches the specified threshold and continue daily until the monthly usage period resets or you adjust the spending policy.

claims.claim: Deleting a policy does not remove, reallocate or reset Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Deleting a spending policy doesn't remove, reallocate, or reset Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: After deletion, users continue under another policy that applies through their group membership.
claims.quote: If another spending policy applies to a user through group membership, the user continues to consume Copilot Credits under the applicable policy.

claims.claim: Cost Management's Overview tab refreshes every four hours.
claims.quote: The Overview tab refreshes every 4 hours.

claims.claim: The Consumption tab refreshes every two hours.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab refreshes every 2 hours.

claims.claim: Consumption reports usage by spending policy, user, group, agent and service.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab provides reporting experiences for copilot credit usage by: ... Spending policy ... User ... Group ... Agent ... Service

claims.claim: Consumption reporting includes spending-limit utilisation.
claims.quote: Limit utilization: Credit usage divided by the current spending limit.

claims.claim: Administrators review users' credit requests on the Credit requests page.
claims.quote: To view and approve credit requests from end users, select View requests. The Credit requests page displays all pending and approved requests.

claims.claim: No spending-policy PowerShell cmdlet is documented in the material searched.
claims.quote: Searched: "spendingPolicies" "PowerShell" Copilot; Copilot spending policy activate default policy API PowerShell resource-based environments Graph. Read Graph overview/create/update/list and Studio costs; results document REST operations, not spending-policy PowerShell cmdlets.

claims.claim: The pages read do not give identity-policy limit-change propagation time; the 12-minute figure concerns linking environments to resource policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot spending policies credit rates identity based limit change take effect timing. Read managing credits, setup and Studio costs: editing says Save changes applies updates without a duration; only linking an environment is assigned up to 12 minutes.
